analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1–805) and the supplied bounded patch. In this excerpt scope, the changes are a date update and a HEAD line 156 command-table entry introducing `addon status/hold/release`; the patch also begins new documentation at HEAD lines 904 onward. Documentation alone does not establish a missing control or exploitable regression. No supported finding is identified.
The surrounding BASE documents coordinator authorization, encrypted SSD cache opt-out/storage constraints (lines 37–88; T-041), model-switch validation and routing/usage barriers (328–389; T-012/T-027, A-009), drain and native-owner retirement (410–448; T-010/T-029), issuer-bound logout and confirmed process exit (532–581; A-008/T-053), and App Attest versus legacy enrollment (673–687; T-052/T-057). These controls are not changed in the displayed ranges.
Integration should examine AddonCommand.swift and the add-on mailbox/socket implementation referenced by the new documentation: verify owner-only access, live-process binding, hold/release bounds and cleanup, and whether holds interfere with idle unloading, memory admission, model switching, graceful shutdown or logout. Relevant boundaries are TB-003/TB-007 and availability threat T-029. The socket is new documented local attack surface, not evidence of unauthorized access. The HEAD implementation, full new section (904–932), and additional HEAD change at 1758 are absent here; remaining security conclusions about add-on behavior require the other PR units. Only selected canonical definitions were supplied in full.
